title: TS SDK: async iterator ↔ Web Streams hybrid patterns walkthrough
creator: Anika Patel
description: Create a focused engineering ticket to design, implement, and ship a concise set of TypeScript SDK primitives and end-to-end examples that demonstrate reliable interop between AsyncIterable (for Node/TS consumers) and WHATWG ReadableStream/Web Streams (for browser & Deno). The goal is to offer a minimal, well-documented API surface that handles cancellation, backpressure, streaming errors, and resumable reads across runtime boundaries. Deliverables include small helper APIs, comprehensive examples (Node server, browser client, deno/edge worker), unit + integration tests, and a short guidance doc for application developers and internal SDK reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Expose two stable helpers: toAsyncIterable(stream, options) and toWebReadable(asyncIterable, options) with TS types and clear AbortSignal handling
Examples for three environments: Node (ReadableStream from fetch/llm), Browser client using fetch stream, Deno/Edge worker using native Web Streams
Cancellation semantics: cancel on consumer AbortSignal, propagate cancellation to underlying network/connection, and surface errors to both sides
Backpressure: demonstrate buffering limits and resource cleanup in example apps; performance baseline tests added
Docs: short walkthrough in SDK repo docs with snippets and migration notes; a PR merged with code owner reviews
Tests: unit tests covering stream-to-iterator conversions, cancellation, mid-stream error propagation, and multiple concurrent consumers where allowed
tasks: Design API surface and options (bufferSize, preferPull/push, abort propagation)
Implement helpers in ts-sdk core runtime module with minimal runtime deps
Write three example apps (node-server.ts, browser-client.html, deno-worker.ts)
Add Jest/unit tests + small e2e harness using local mock server
Create docs page and migration guide referencing existing streaming primitives
Open PR, address reviewer feedback, and cut release note blurb
updates: 2026-02-12 — Spike complete: validated patterns converting ReadableStream->AsyncIterable using built-in async iterator support in Node 20 and Deno. Found one subtlety: Node ReadableStream implementations do not always propagate AbortSignal to underlying fetch; added explicit signal wiring in helpers.
2026-02-20 — Decision: keep helpers minimal and opt-in. Do not change existing public streaming surfaces. Expose helpers in 'streaming-utils' namespace and mark as stable for 2026.03 release.
2026-02-27 — Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1842. Basic conversions implemented plus example for browser fetch streaming. Requesting primary reviewers: @mlee, @sarah-chen.
2026-03-03 — Review notes from @sarah-chen: add tests for double cancellation (consumer aborts while network aborts) and document behavior when underlying runtime lacks signal propagation.
2026-03-07 — Implemented AbortSignal chaining and added tests. Found race where mid-chunk error sometimes swallowed; fixed by forwarding error events and ensuring async iterators throw on next().
2026-03-11 — Performance microbenchmark added: conversion cost ~120ns per token on Node 20 with small buffer; acceptable but document tuning knobs for high-throughput use cases.
2026-03-13 — Ready for final review: examples cleaned, docs drafted, PR updated with fixes. Assigned to Marcus for final approvals and merge coordination. Release note draft attached.
notes: Compatibility note: ensure helpers are tree-shakeable and do not pull in fetch polyfills by default
UX choice: do not attempt to multiplex a single AsyncIterable to multiple Web Streams; document recommended fan-out patterns
Edge case: in browsers where ReadableStream.getReader() is used, ensure to release lock on early cancellation to avoid memory leak
Suggested follow-up: a separate ticket to add TypeScript-first typed streaming responses (structured output) that pairs with these primitives
